title: Autosomal Recessive Polycystic Kidney Disease: PKHD1, Fibrocystin and Portal Hypertension
subject: ss-paediatric-nephrology
module: Tubular Disorders, Cystic Diseases and Stones

steps.say: Mutations in the PKHD1 gene encoding fibrocystin cause autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease and ductal plate malformations.
steps.tx: Examine the molecular genetics underlying **PKHD1 fibrocystin genetics** in presenting families. Autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease (ARPKD) is caused by mutations in the PKHD1 gene located on chromosome 6p12.3-p12.2. PKHD1 encodes fibrocystin (also known as polyductin), a large receptor-like membrane protein localized to the primary cilia and basal body of renal collecting duct epithelia and biliary tract cholangiocytes.

vis.title: PKHD1 Genetic and Molecular Characteristics
rows: Essential for ciliary structure and planar polarity
Disruption drives collecting duct and biliary ectasia
Two truncating alleles produce lethal neonatal disease

steps.say: Massive bilateral nephromegaly and oligohydramnios produce classic Potter sequence and severe pulmonary hypoplasia in neonates.
steps.tx: Recognize the life-threatening neonatal manifestations of **Potter sequence and pulmonary hypoplasia** at delivery. Severe antenatal ARPKD presentation features massive symmetric bilateral nephromegaly, marked oligohydramnios from reduced fetal urine output, Potter sequence (compressed flat facial features, low-set ears, clubbed feet), pulmonary hypoplasia, and a thirty percent neonatal mortality rate primarily caused by respiratory insufficiency.

steps.say: High-resolution ultrasonography demonstrates symmetrically enlarged echogenic kidneys with radial acoustic shadowing.
steps.tx: Evaluate characteristic imaging features to identify the **Ultrasound spoke-wheel appearance** in pediatric patients. High-resolution renal ultrasonography demonstrates massively enlarged, symmetric, highly echogenic kidneys with poor corticomedullary differentiation. Millions of microscopic cylindrical dilated collecting ducts oriented radially from the medulla to the cortex create acoustic interfaces resembling a spoke-wheel or salt-and-pepper pattern.

steps.say: All patients with autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease have concomitant congenital hepatic fibrosis.
steps.tx: Screen for hepatobiliary complications reflecting **Congenital hepatic fibrosis (CHF) pairing** across childhood follow-up. All patients with ARPKD have concomitant congenital hepatic fibrosis resulting from abnormal development of the embryonic ductal plate. Children surviving the neonatal period present in childhood with portal hypertension, severe splenomegaly, hypersplenism, and bleeding gastroesophageal varices.

right.title: Hepatic Predominance (Late)
points: Ductal plate malformation and portal fibrosis

steps.say: Non-obstructive intrahepatic cystic biliary dilatation predisposes to life-threatening ascending bacterial cholangitis.
steps.tx: Recognize the presentation and management of **Caroli disease and bacterial cholangitis** in affected children. Non-obstructive cystic dilatation of the intrahepatic bile ducts (Caroli disease or Caroli syndrome when combined with congenital hepatic fibrosis) predisposes to biliary stasis, lithiasis, and recurrent ascending bacterial cholangitis. Acute episodes demand intravenous antibiotics, and recurrent disease warrants prophylactic co-trimoxazole or cephalosporins.

vis.title: Caroli Syndrome Complications and Care
rows: Fever, right upper quadrant pain, elevated CRP
Intraductal calculi on liver ultrasound / MRCP

steps.say: Severe early-onset systemic hypertension develops in over eighty percent of children, requiring aggressive multidrug therapy.
steps.tx: Control cardiovascular risk through management of **Severe early-onset systemic hypertension** from the first months of life. Over eighty percent of children with ARPKD develop severe hypertension in the first months of life due to intrarenal ischemia and hyper-reninemia secondary to tubular compression. Blood pressure management requires aggressive multi-drug therapy with angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors (such as enalapril) and calcium channel blockers (amlodipine).

steps.say: Hepatic synthetic function remains completely normal in uncomplicated congenital hepatic fibrosis despite massive portal hypertension.
steps.tx: Identify the critical laboratory finding of **Preserved liver synthetic function hallmark** to distinguish CHF from cirrhosis. Despite severe portal hypertension, massive splenomegaly, and bleeding esophageal varices, hepatic synthetic function (measured by serum albumin, serum bilirubin, and prothrombin time / international normalized ratio) remains completely normal in uncomplicated congenital hepatic fibrosis, because hepatocytes are structurally uninjured.

vis.title: Liver Function Profile in Uncomplicated CHF

steps.say: Combined liver and kidney transplantation is indicated for patients with kidney failure and severe hepatic complications.
steps.tx: Evaluate surgical indications to recommend **Combined liver-kidney transplantation criteria** in advanced multisystem disease. Dual-organ combined liver-kidney transplantation is indicated in patients reaching end-stage renal disease who have concomitant recurrent life-threatening ascending bacterial cholangitis, intractable gastroesophageal variceal bleeding refractory to endoscopic therapy, or severe hypersplenism.
